'''Antoni "Toni" Lima Solà''' (born 22 September 1970) is a former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[central defender]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Gavà]], [[Province of Barcelona|Barcelona]], [[Catalonia]] to an Andalusian father<!-- from Málaga --> and a Catalan mother<!-- from Gavà -->,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariandorra.ad/noticies/dmg/amb_cara_ulls/2019/04/07/ildefons_lima_mapamundi_144192_1173.html|title=Ildefons Lima i el mapamundi|trans-title=Ildefons Lima and the world map|newspaper=[[Diari d'Andorra]]|first=Alba|last=Doral|language=ca|date=7 April 2019|access-date=29 December 2019|archive-date=29 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191229114416/https://www.diariandorra.ad/noticies/dmg/amb_cara_ulls/2019/04/07/ildefons_lima_mapamundi_144192_1173.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Lima's family moved to Andorra when he was nine years old.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aKrA78HA_5Q&t=103|title=Fiebre Maldini: Ildefons Lima, orgullo de Andorra {{!}} Movistar+|trans-title=Fiebre Maldini: Ildefons Lima, pride of Andorra {{!}} Movistar+|via=[[YouTube]]|language=es|access-date=29 December 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/aKrA78HA_5Q|archive-date=21 December 2021}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

==Club career==
Lima had a brief spell with [[Real Madrid Castilla]], then signed with [[RCD Espanyol|RCD Español]], for which he played two [[La Liga]] games.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1991/10/28/pagina-10/1249446/pdf.html|title=Otro aire, pero los mismos fallos|trans-title=Another allure, but the same mistakes|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=M.C.|last=Canovas|language=es|date=28 October 1991|access-date=3 June 2016|archive-date=30 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160630030214/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1991/10/28/pagina-10/1249446/pdf.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1991/11/04/pagina-12/1243392/pdf.html|title=Sarrià se levanta en armas|trans-title=Sarrià is up in arms|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Andrés|last=Astruells|language=es|date=4 November 1991|access-date=3 June 2016|archive-date=30 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160630025821/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1991/11/04/pagina-12/1243392/pdf.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In 1992, he stayed in his native region and spent three seasons with [[Palamós CF]] in the [[Segunda División]], being [[1994–95 Segunda División|relegated in the last]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1995/06/12/deportes/802908040_850215.html|title=Adiós con derrota|trans-title=Goodbye with loss|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Pere|last=Subirana|language=es|date=12 June 1995|access-date=4 January 2023|archive-date=4 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230104103139/https://elpais.com/diario/1995/06/12/deportes/802908040_850215.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

After [[1995–96 Segunda División|another season in the second division]], with [[CP Almería]], Lima spent the remainder of his Spanish career in the [[Segunda División B]] or lower. He also had two abroad experiences: in 1998 he joined [[C.F. União]], appearing rarely as the [[Segunda Liga|Portuguese second-tier]] team was also [[1998–99 Segunda Divisão de Honra|relegated]]. Three years later, also with no impact whatsoever, he represented [[Ionikos F.C.]] in the [[Super League Greece]].<ref name=BD>{{cite news|url=https://www.bondia.ad/esports/dels-red-devils-el-glorioso|title=Dels The Red Devils a 'El Glorioso'|trans-title=From the Red Devils to 'The Glorious One'|newspaper=[[Bondia (newspaper)|Bondia]]|first=Víctor|last=Duaso|language=ca|date=28 June 2019|access-date=4 January 2023|archive-date=4 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230104102245/https://www.bondia.ad/esports/dels-red-devils-el-glorioso|url-status=live}}</ref>

Lima retired at [[UD Ibiza-Eivissa|SE Eivissa-Ibiza]] in 2008 at the age of 37, having acted as the club's [[director of football]] still as an active player.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.infobalear.com/actualidad/detallenoticia.cgi?codigo=29204&tipo=portal|title=El Murcia cede al Eivissa al ariete Pico|trans-title=Murcia loan forward Pico to Eivissa|publisher=Info Balear|first1=C.|last1=Vidal|first2=R. J.|last2=Palomo|language=es|date=29 January 2008|access-date=3 June 2016|archive-date=28 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180728035826/http://www.infobalear.com/actualidad/detallenoticia.cgi?codigo=29204&tipo=portal|url-status=live}}</ref> He later worked with [[Premier League]] sides [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] as well as [[Inter Milan]] of [[Serie A]] as [[Scout (association football)|scout]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/futbol-internacional/arsenal-ficha-toni-lima-descubridor-11998054|title=El Arsenal ficha a Toni Lima, descubridor de Neymar y Coutinho en Europa|trans-title=Arsenal sign Toni Lima, finder of Neymar and Coutinho in Europe|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|language=es|date=17 August 2021|access-date=4 January 2023|archive-date=4 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230104095132/https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/futbol-internacional/arsenal-ficha-toni-lima-descubridor-11998054|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=BD/> and [[Deportivo Alavés]] as director of international football.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.noticiasdealava.eus/alaves/2019/06/28/lima-nuevo-responsable-area-internacional-1256898.html|title=Lima, nuevo responsable del Área Internacional|trans-title=Lima, new man in charge of International Department|newspaper=Noticias de Álava|language=es|date=28 June 2019|access-date=4 January 2023|archive-date=4 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230104102221/https://www.noticiasdealava.eus/alaves/2019/06/28/lima-nuevo-responsable-area-internacional-1256898.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==International career==
Lima won 64 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Andorra national football team|Andorra]] over a 12-year period.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/alima-intl.html|title=Antonio Lima Solá – International Appearances|website=[[RSSSF]]|first=Roberto|last=Mamrud|access-date=3 June 2016}}</ref> On 10 June 2009, in his last international, a 6–0 loss to [[England national football team|England]] for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|qualifiers]] at [[Wembley Stadium]], he wore the [[Captain (association football)|captain]]'s armband.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/soccer/2009-06-10-3011605702_x.htm|title=Andorra loses 6–0 to England but prevents ridicule|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|first=Frank|last=Griffiths|date=10 June 2009|access-date=6 May 2015}}</ref>

In September 2005, Lima was subject of some controversy during a [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group 1|World Cup qualification match]] against the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]]. When [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]] missed a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]], the defender celebrated directly in front of the Dutch player. Moments later, the striker scored from open play and ran straight over to Lima with his arms raised, being [[Fouls and misconduct (association football)|booked]] for his action in an eventual 4–0 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/soccer/the-seven-levels-of-soccer-vengeance/|title=The seven levels of soccer vengeance|publisher=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]|first=Taylor|last=Rockwell|date=5 June 2014|access-date=8 February 2021|archive-date=31 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031003107/https://www.pastemagazine.com/soccer/the-seven-levels-of-soccer-vengeance/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.planetfootball.com/trending/haalands-sht-talking-is-not-a-patch-on-van-nistelrooys-revenge-celebration/|title=Haaland's sh*t-talking is not a patch on Van Nistelrooy's revenge celebration|publisher=Planet Football|first=Nathan|last=Egerton|date=10 March 2021|access-date=26 March 2021|archive-date=23 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423084310/https://www.planetfootball.com/trending/haalands-sht-talking-is-not-a-patch-on-van-nistelrooys-revenge-celebration/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Lima's younger brother, [[Ildefons Lima|Ildefons]], is also a footballer and a defender. He too spent most of his career in the lower leagues of Spain, and the pair shared teams at Ionikos.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://arogeraldes.blogspot.pt/2007/02/andorra-el-milagro-contra-macedonia.html|title=Andorra – El milagro contra Macedonia|trans-title=Andorra – The miracle against Macedonia|publisher=Pablo Aro Geraldes|language=es|date=3 February 2007|access-date=3 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.am14.net/ildefons-lima-de-andorra-wembley/|title=Ildefons Lima, un andorrano en Wembley|trans-title=Ildefons Lima, an Andorran in Wembley|publisher=AM 14|first=Jordi|last=Blanco|language=es|date=13 November 2014|access-date=3 June 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160625181436/http://www.am14.net/ildefons-lima-de-andorra-wembley/|archive-date=25 June 2016}}</ref>
